layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Connectivity in Medical Tubular Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Qian Wu®, Yufei Chen, Wei Liu®, Xiaodong Yue®, and Xiahai Zhuang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—Accurately segmenting tubular structures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as blood vessels or nerves, holds significant clinical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implications across various medical applications. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: existing methods often exhibit limitations in achieving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfactory topological performance, particularly in terms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of preserving connectivity. To address this challenge,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we propose a novel deep-learning approach, termed Deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Closing, inspired by the well-established classic closing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operation. Deep Closing first leverages an AutoEncoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained in the Masked Image Modeling (MIM) paradigm,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhanced with digital topology knowledge, to effectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learn the inherent shape prior of tubular structures and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicate potential disconnected regions. Subsequently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a Simple Components Erosion module is employed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate topology-focused outcomes, which refines the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preceding segmentation results, ensuring all the generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regions are topologically significant. To evaluate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficacy of Deep Closing, we conduct comprehensive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experiments on 4 datasets: DRIVE, CHASE_DB1, DCA1, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CREMI. The results demonstrate that our approach yields

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considerable improvements in topological performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared with existing methods. Furthermore, Deep Clos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing exhibits the ability to generalize and transfer knowledge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from external datasets, showcasing its robustness and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adaptability. The code for this paper has been available at:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: https://github.com/5k5000/DeepClosing.

layout_dets.text: I. INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: UBULAR structures constitute significant anatomical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: .features present in various medical images, encompassing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entities such as blood vessels and airways. Despite the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remarkable achievements of deep learning methodologies in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation [1], [2], the segmentation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tubular structures remains a formidable endeavor, largely due

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to their intricate morphologies and diverse scales [3], [4].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An illustration of the Classic Closing Operation and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed Deep Closing. The traditional closing operation compromises

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two steps: Dilation and Erosion, which first generate new foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points alongside borders and then eliminate part of them with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predetermined kernels. Correspondingly, our approach introduces two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhanced constituents: Deep Dilation, which involves the indication of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disconnection regions through the reconstruction process of a masked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AutoEncoder (MAE) embedded with tubular shape prior; and Simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Component Erosion to filter out topologically insignificant regions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It often encounters challenges in preserving continuity within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diminutive and low signal-to-noise regions, thereby risking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the disruption of structural topology. This issue predominantly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emerges from the substantial intra-class variance apparent in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel-level features within these localized regions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The issue of connectivity defects in medical tubular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures is somewhat different from those in general

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks where the models typically aim to achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better overlapping-based performance, i.e. higher Dice score.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The disconnected regions tend to appear in thin and tiny

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parts which may have minimal effects on the overall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overlapping-oriented optimization, thus usually causing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem of disconnection under-focused. To surmount this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenge, some researchers have designed topology-aware

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods [5], [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [11] which typically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impose extra topological constraints or networks designs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during optimization. Some propose to enhance topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance based on label refinement [12], [13], [14] which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typically cascades multiple networks and makes the following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ones serve as label error fixers for preceding ones. Besides,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some general post-processing methods for segmentation like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ConvCRF [15], CascadePSP [16] and Segrefiner [17], also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: show some effectiveness in mitigating the disconnection issue.

layout_dets.text: WU et al.: DEEP CLOSING: ENHANCING TOPOLOGICAL CONNECTIVITY IN MEDICAL TUBULAR SEGMENTATION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The limitations of topology-aware methods, label refinement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques, and post-processing strategies in medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, particularly for tubular structures, present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unique challenges. Topology-aware methods, despite incorpo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rating topological constraints, are predominantly guided by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overlapping-based segmentation loss in an end-to-end training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pattern. This dominance of segmentation loss means that any

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvements in topological performance could be inherently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited, as the primary optimization direction remains focused

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on segmentation accuracy. Label refinement methods carry the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: risk of overfitting specific refinement criteria, limiting their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalizability to other models and making them primarily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applicable only to the original models that they were trained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with. Post-processing methods, while effective in the context

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of natural images, tend to underperform when applied to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical tubular datasets. This ineffectiveness is often due to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the specialized nature of medical images, where the structural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complexity and the critical importance of accurate topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present challenges that standard post-processing techniques

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cannot handle.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address the above challenges, we aim to design a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape-oriented connectivity-enhancing method that is model-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agnostic, generalizable, and can perform even when source

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images are unavailable. Following this purpose, we turn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our attention to the classic closing operation, a technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specifically designed to bridge minor gaps within shapes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The Closing operation constitutes a foundational technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within image processing, assuming particular significance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within the field of both medical image and natural image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis. However, on the one hand, the judicious choice of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structuring elements like kernel size in the closing operation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assumes paramount importance, as an improperly chosen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size may result in insufficient gap closure or unintended

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amalgamation and smoothing of neighboring structures. On the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other hand, though easy to implement and generalizable,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the performance of this conventional technique is essentially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Motivated by this, we propose a novel deep learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach that extends the traditional closing operation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as shown in Fig.1. We replace the dilation process with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruction of a designed Masked AutoEncoder, called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Deep Dilation, and the erosion process with the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Simple Component Erosion operation. This approach leverages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pre-trained knowledge to learn the intrinsic shape prior of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tubular structures and focuses on the connectivity information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to identify and refine the segmentation results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our contributions are summarized as follows: (1) As

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generally shown in Fig. 1, we propose a novel paradigm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that revisits the classic closing operation with deep learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques to enhance connectivity in the segmentation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical tubular structures. (2) We design a Simple Point

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Erosion module based on Digital Topology knowledge, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could efficiently deplete points that will not affect the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology under a paralleled pipeline, hereby identifying the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topologically critical ones. This module could be integrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into the proposed framework and provide enhanced topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guidance. (3) Our extensive experiments demonstrate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectiveness of improving topological performance and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transferability of our approach to learn from external datasets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancing overall segmentation performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: II. RELATED WORKS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Topology-Aware Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Deep Learning methods have achieved huge success in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical segmentation [1], [18], [19], [20], [21], and most of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them are optimized towards better overlap between prediction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and target. However, in such a setting, topological coherence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is often attached with less significance during optimization as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it contributes little to the overall performance when measured

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with overlap-based metrics, such as Dice and IOU [9].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To improve the topological performance in tubular struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, some researchers propose adding topological constraints

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during optimization in order to guide models to focus on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserving topology. The core idea of these methods is to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: identify a group of topologically critical points and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impose an extra penalty on them. Hu et al. [5] first propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to utilize the persistence diagram to enforce the topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency between the prediction and ground truth. After

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that, they propose Discrete Morse Theory (DMT) Loss [6]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which uses the Morse complex of the likelihood map

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to generate skeletons as topological constraints with time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complexity of O(nlog(n)). They later simplify the critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points searching process with an efficient homotopy warping

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operation [7], theoretically achieving a time complexity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: O(n). However, it's worth noting that while this technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: offers advantages, it may not always guarantee the identifica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of all topologically critical points and involves operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that can be computationally intensive on CPUs, such as depth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distance transform and pixel-wise loops. The authors of [9]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propose a novel, efficient, and differentiable skeletonization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach, called Centerline Dice (Cldice). They further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduce an additional loss on the computed centerlines of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prediction and labels, in order to emphasize connectivity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, their proposed skeletonization approach represents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an approximation and may result in disconnected segments on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centerlines. Stucki et al. [22] point out that the Wasserstein

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matching adopted in [5] could not always guarantee spatially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correct matching and introduce a Betti Matching method to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address such issue.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Beyond designing pixel-level topological constrains,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hu et al. [8] also pioneer another branch of methods in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning probabilistic topological representation, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could perform structure-level sampling, together with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uncertainty, thus leading to better topological integrity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gupta et al. [23] design a more fine-grained probabilistic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural representation learning by introducing a probabilistic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DMT model, and further consider both inter-structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and intra-structure uncertainty, yielding more promising

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uncertainty maps.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PointScatter [10] designs a point prediction and regression

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paradigm for tubular structure segmentation, which could

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be utilized as an auxiliary task and embedded into existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods, in order to enhance topological performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DconnNet [11] decouples directional features from the shared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subspace via enforcing the model to predict a connectivity map

layout_dets.text: B. Enhancing Topological Performance via Label

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Refinement and Post-Processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To enhance the topological performance, another approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is to conduct a secondary analysis of the pre-computed results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using post-processing methods [24], [25], [26], [27]. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods introduce additional topological constraints to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: likelihood maps. In recent years, researchers have also adopted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deep learning-based approaches to develop multi-stage or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cascaded methods for improving topological performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One such method, DoubleUnet [13], combines two UNet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [1] structures and implicitly embeds the target of topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancement into the overall optimization process. Another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach, DVAE-refiner [12], proposes cascading a denoising

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) after a typical segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network. The VAE module first encodes precomputed shapes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a compact latent space and then reconstructs new ones

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to yield refined results. ErrorNet [14] cascades a noise-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: injected VAE to synthesize label errors and then trains another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional network to learn the synthetic error residue.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During the inference stage, ErrorNet fuses segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results and error-corrected regions to yield better overall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outcomes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. Masked Image Modeling & Denoising AutoEncoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, the autoregressive paradigm of masking and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruction has garnered significant attention from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: researchers in the field of computer vision. Notable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contributions in this area include BEiT [29], MAE [30],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Simmim [31]. While these works primarily focus on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretraining Transformer architectures [32], [33], we have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discovered that the technique of masking images can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapted and modified to efficiently generate synthetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disconnected errors for tubular structures. Denoising

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AutoEncoders are neural networks that are trained to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruct clean data from noisy or corrupted inputs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By introducing a masking mechanism, where certain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regions of the input are intentionally masked or corrupted,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denoising AutoEncoders can learn to effectively recover

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the missing or corrupted information. This approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has shown promising results in various applications,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including image denoising, inpainting, and now, in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generation of synthetic disconnected errors for tubular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we first introduce the basic concepts of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Definition 1: (Simple Point [7], [34]). A pixel in a binary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image is considered a simple point if it can be inverted from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point only requires analyzing its surrounding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we utilize the property of simple points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to distinguish topologically significant points from others.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, it can be utilized as a method of thinning to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate a diverse range of tubular structures without altering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the topology, serving as an efficient way of data augmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hu et al. [7] introduce an algorithm designed to gradually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eliminate simple points within a structure. This approach is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimized using greedy strategies and theoretically reach a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time complexity of O(n), with n representing the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels. However, there are certain considerations to keep in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mind: (1) The nature of approximation employed by these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategies may present challenges when attempting to filter out

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all simple points. (2) Furthermore, the sequential computing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aspect, including the need for connected component analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for each pixel, could potentially result in computational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inefficiency when integrated into deep learning frameworks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In response to these challenges, we propose an efficient

layout_dets.text: D. Comparing With the Segmentation Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We first construct a series of segmentation methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: benchmarks. Among these methods, Cldice [9], TopoLoss [5],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: WarpingLoss [7], PointScatter [10], DconnNet [11] are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology-aware segmentation methods, and DoubleUNet [13],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DVAE_refiner [12], ErrorNet [14] are label-refinement based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To assess the extent of improvement brought about by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our proposed method, we employ it as a post-processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach to enhance the performance of the aforementioned

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: benchmarks. By integrating our method into the pipeline,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we aim to demonstrate its ability to refine and enhance the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation results obtained from these existing techniques.

layout_dets.text: V. CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose a post-processing method that effectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: identifies potential disconnected regions in tubular structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While end-to-end approaches are currently favored, we believe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our method holds significant value for the following reasons:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) Our method has the potential to further improve the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological performance of existing end-to-end methods. (2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In situations where privacy concerns or limited data acces-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sibility prevent access to the original data, our method can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produce enhanced outcomes via analyzing shape information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alone. (3) Unlike end-to-end approaches, our method generates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: new topologically critical regions without altering the original

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: output. This makes it more explainable and suitable for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interactive diagnosis. (4) Even when both image and label data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are inaccessible, our method can transfer the learned inherent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape prior from other datasets to the target field.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we introduce a novel framework that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: redefines traditional morphological closing operations through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the integration of advanced deep learning techniques.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our approach utilizes the reconstruction capabilities of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained masked AutoEncoder, which we term Deep Dilation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to effectively highlight areas of disconnection. Additionally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we have developed a module called Simple Point Erosion,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aimed at identifying topologically critical points by selectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eroding non-essential ones (simple points). This further leads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the design of a novel operation, Simple Component Erosion,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designed to eliminate topologically insignificant components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our proposed framework comprises these two innovative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operations. It demonstrates significant potential in identifying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regions of disconnection, thereby enhancing the topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of medical tubular segmentation. Moreover,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our method exhibits a strong capability to transfer shape

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: priors from external datasets, showcasing its versatility and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectiveness across different applications.
